summary.headline: Bikaji Q4 FY26 revenue grew close to 18% to about INR720 crores, with FY26 revenue of INR2,994 crores and 9.5% volume growth.
summary.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 top-line growth of close to 18%, with revenue from operations around INR720 crores, EBITDA about INR88 crores (roughly 12.2% margin) and PAT about INR56 crores. For FY26, revenue was about INR2,994 crores on 9.5% volume growth, with consolidated gross margin of 35.1% and EBITDA margin of 13.7%, up over 120 bps. Q4 EBITDA was pressured by a step-up in advertising linked to the Bhujia and Kya Baat Hai Ji campaigns, plus a Bengal-election labour exodus and a 2.5-day factory shutdown. Management took a price rise of about 3% in April 2026 to offset edible oil and packaging inflation.

segments.name: Ethnic snacks
segments.commentary: Q4 volume growth in line with overall volume growth of 16.1%; FY26 ethnic snacks growth stated at 11%. Bhujia (Bikaji brand) campaign drove strong H2 momentum.

segments.name: Western snacks
segments.commentary: Q4 growth about 8.5% YoY versus 25% in Q3; FY26 about 7%. Management targets 20%+ growth and lifting Western share of business from 8.5% to about 11% in 3 years.

segments.name: Sweets
segments.commentary: FY26 growth about 9% against a target of 11-12%; budgeted at about 12.5% for the year. A new Bikaner sweets factory is being built; capacity is constrained in festive months (about 80% of sweets sales fall in four months from Rakhi to Diwali).

segments.name: Family pack and impulse
segments.commentary: Family pack grew about 20% in Q4 and impulse about 14%. Family pack price was raised and impulse grammage cut.

segments.name: Packaged food and brand
segments.commentary: Bikaji brand revenue crossed INR100 crores in FY26, with a target of 50-60% growth annually for 2-3 years.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance: core states growth about 13% plus or minus, focus states growth about 20%; management said 15% growth would not be sustainable.
Consolidated gross margin target is to maintain FY26 level (35.1%) in FY27; EBITDA expected to improve through fixed-cost leverage and CMU (co-manufacturing) output.
Advertising budget for FY27 held at about 2% of sales, same as last year.
Capex of close to INR100 crores planned in FY27, including a sweets factory in Bikaner.
THF plans to open 8-10 stores a year for 3 years and grow top line 50-55%; Bikaji retail to open 2 outlets in next 6 months.
Ariba (frozen) utilisation expected to rise to about 55-60% to make it EBITDA-neutral; export growth expected at 50-60%.
capex_capacity: Capex of close to INR100 crores planned this year, mainly a sweets factory in Bikaner; capacity added in FY26 was limited.
New warehouse adjacent to the plant: trials began about two weeks before the call, full operations from about 15 June 2026; storage rises from under 2 days of finished goods to 6-8 days.
Outlet reach reached 3.5 lakh direct outlets (about 1.2 lakh core, 1.7 lakh focus, 0.6 lakh other states); indirect reach about 8.2 lakh in core, 1.8 lakh in other states.
Production shift from Bikaner to co-manufacturing units (CMU) expected to add operational efficiency in FY27.
Sweets capacity at 100%+ utilisation in festive months but very low utilisation off-season.
demand_pricing: Price rise of about 3% taken in April 2026; management said it is enough to offset current raw material and packaging inflation and will decide on further hikes depending on the war.
Edible oil costs up about 12-14%; packaging material up about 25-30% at peak, then eased to INR220-225 from INR260-270 per unit cited.
Pulses and flour prices have not seen major increases.
Post-April demand momentum reported as continuing with no slowdown despite the price pass-through.

Bengal election-related migration of workers and a 2.5-day factory shutdown after the Chairman's death cost about 4-4.5 days of production in Q4 and Q1 to date; management said sales were partly lost but demand was not.
Delhi market underperforming; UP growing upwards of 20%, and UP's TAM equals the other five focus states combined.
Management expects regional and local brands to exit under GST rationalisation, with benefits to organised players over 2-4 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why did H2 EBITDA margin fall to about 11% from about 13.5-14% in H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it mainly to advertising, which was about 3.2-3.3% of sales in Q3/Q4 versus about 1% in H1, plus about 50 bps of one-time doubtful-debt provisions in the last two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the difference between consolidated growth of 19% and standalone growth of 15%?
qa_highlights.answer: The gap is mainly THF retail, worth about 2.2 percentage points of growth, with Bikaji USA and Ariba also contributing; management confirmed there is no inorganic contribution this year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 margin outlook and the price hike plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to hold consolidated gross margin at FY26 levels and says EBITDA will improve on fixed-cost leverage and CMU volumes; one price rise of about 3% was taken in April.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sweets growth constraint?
qa_highlights.answer: Sweets is capacity-constrained in festive months and under-utilised off-season; a new Bikaner factory and small all-season SKUs at INR5-10 are planned, with FY27 sweets budgeted at about 12.5% growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlet split and the target for 5 lakh outlets?
qa_highlights.answer: Current direct reach is 3.5 lakh outlets; the next 1.5 lakh are expected mainly from focus states, with core states moving toward direct distribution rather than wholesalers.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Western snacks slow in Q4 and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Western snacks grew about 8.5% in Q4 after 25% in Q3; management attributed it to weaker family-pack traction and a soft category, and expects 20%+ growth going forward from a base of 1.1% national share.

risks_watch: Raw material inflation: edible oil and packaging costs are volatile due to the war; further price increases may be needed to protect gross margin.
Advertising intensity: FY27 ad spend held at about 2%, but H2 margins were pressured by campaign spend, and campaigns must be refreshed each cycle.
Western snacks growth slowed to about 8.5% in Q4 and needs to recover to the 20%+ target.
Delhi underperformance and weaker focus-state execution; the 1.5x focus-market growth aspiration was not met in FY26.
Q1 FY27 impact from labour shortage after Bengal elections and the factory's new warehouse ramp-up (targeted 15 June 2026).
Sweets capacity additions carry utilisation risk outside the festive season.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and distribution, with a clear FY27 framework and price actions, but cautious on input costs, which management called fluctuating and dependent on the war. Management was candid about the Q4 margin dip, attributing it to advertising and one-time provisions, and gave direct answers on Western snacks and Delhi weakness.

growth.why: FY27 guidance is core-state growth of about 13% plus/minus and focus-state growth of about 20%, with Q4 revenue up close to 18%; backing is partial, with a Bikaner sweets factory (~INR100 cr capex, timing not stated), a 3% price rise and maintained gross margin, but no firm capacity or order numbers for the total growth guide.
